summary: Information systems come in several types and are built through an SDLC under a chosen model; each model trades predictability for flexibility.
CASE tools, SOA and OOAD/UML are supporting technologies; agile methods and XP emphasise short iterations.
Software may be built, bought, outsourced or reused; the project manager schedules with Gantt charts and the critical path method.

summary: Projects are identified from many sources and selected with explicit criteria aligned to corporate strategy.
Initiation sets up the team, charter, scope and management procedures.
Feasibility tests, especially cost-benefit measures (NPV, ROI, payback), decide whether to proceed.
The baseline project plan is reviewed by walkthrough and becomes the standard for later phases.

summary: Requirements are gathered by interviews, questionnaires, observation, documents, JAD, prototyping and, in agile projects, user stories; BPR rethinks processes.
DFDs model processes in levels with strict rules and balancing; decision tables, structured English and trees model complex logic.
Conceptual data models use E-R notation with supertypes, subtypes, business rules and reusable patterns.

summary: Logical design normalises user views, converts E-R diagrams to relations and merges them.
Physical design chooses field formats, tables, file organisations and indexes, trading storage and update cost for speed.
Forms and reports follow consistent, logical, accurate-and-usable guidelines and are assessed with usability testing.
Interface and dialogue design uses the interaction method suited to the user, consistent GUI controls and clear feedback and error messages.

summary: Implementation covers coding, multi-level testing, installation, documentation, training and support, and must manage organisational change.
Installation strategies trade risk against cost; documentation serves maintainers and users.
Maintenance (corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive) is the longest and costliest phase, governed by change control and configuration management.
